paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The Lord's Supper is not a snack break. Jesus took the bread and the cup and said, "do this in remembrance of Me" (1 Corinthians 11:24-25). Every time we eat and drink, Paul says we "proclaim the Lord's death until He comes" (1 Corinthians 11:26), so this table points straight at Jesus.

Now here's why Corinth got a no-praise letter. Their gatherings were full of people grabbing their own meal while someone else sat hungry (1 Corinthians 11:21). Paul says that treats the church of God with contempt and humiliates those who have nothing (1 Corinthians 11:22). If the table is about Jesus giving Himself for us, then showing up and looking out only for me is the opposite of the whole point. That's why Paul says, "wait for one another" (1 Corinthians 11:33).

So what do you do with this, baker? Take the Paul's advice and "examine himself" before the bread and the cup (1 Corinthians 11:28). I'd do it like checking the oven before I load the tray: slow, honest, and before the cookies go in. And if the Lord does correct us, Paul calls it discipline, so we won't be condemned with the world (1 Corinthians 11:32). That's not a Father slamming the door. That's a Father who wants us at the table, together.
